01 · Personality

The reason sits beside the pick.

edh.wtf is the only Commander house whose tools run from the collection to the deck box, where every tool that makes a pick says why and where to check it.

How it looks

The tool's own output is the design. A result reads like a printed pick list: the card name, the reason in plain words, the price at the right edge, and a line under the list with the total behind it. The brand shows that list wherever another brand would show a picture, because the reason beside the pick is the thing edh.wtf does that others do not. Card names, counts and prices are set in a mono face (font.family.display), the way the tool prints them, so columns line up and a number never shifts. Running text is a plain, open sans (font.family.body). Headlines use the mono face at a medium weight; size carries them, not boldness. Corners are softly rounded (radius.sm for buttons, radius.md for panels). Motion is quick and plain (motion.duration.in, motion.easing.ui): a result arrives, it does not perform.

How colour is used

The page is a working surface. In the light theme, ink (color.palette.light.ink) sits on a cool off-white ground (color.palette.light.ground), and results sit on a slightly darker panel (color.palette.light.surface). One blue (color.palette.light.accent, color.palette.dark.accent in the dark theme) marks what to act on and where to go: the primary button, links, the focus ring, the summary rule under a list, and the pick being explained. It never fills a background. The dark theme (color.palette.dark.*) is the result screen at night: a blue-black ground with light ink, and the same blue lifted so it reads on the dark. Players check a build late, after a game, so the dark theme is designed, not inverted.

04 · Logo

The pick you're weighing

Clear space and minimum size

A fanned hand of four cards with the fourth raised out of the hand: the pick you're weighing. It is drawn from rounded rectangles with one constant gap and sits beside the wordmark "edh.wtf" in the mono face. The raised card and the wordmark's period carry the blue accent, the one colour that marks the pick on every page; a one-colour version serves wherever only one colour prints. A separate small drawing, two cards, stands in for it at favicon size. Minimum size: the mark at 48 px, the lockup at 48 px tall. Below 48 px, such as a browser tab, use the small drawing, assets/mark-16.svg; the favicons are built from it. Clear space: a quarter of the mark's height on every side, kept free of type, edges and other marks. On a dark ground use the on-dark files; never recolour the mark in the brand colour on a busy picture.

05 · Voice

Say why, then pass the turn.

Voicetechnical and dry, with proof; the founder's first person, on the About page only
Pairsexact, never smug; dry, never rude; insider, never gatekeeping; flat on rules, never preachy on taste
Person"we" for what we'd run; "you" and "your pod" for the call; the tool is the subject in result lines
Sentencesmostly 8 to 18 words, with the card name, the count or the rule number inside the sentence; one longer sentence where a rule needs explaining
Humourdry, at our own expense or Sol Ring's, in the 404 and empty states only; none in an error that blocks a task
Neverthe suffix written as a word or spelled out; swearing; scarcity or hype words; "the correct build" or "you should" about a pod's choice; praise of ourselves; "users" or "customers"

07 · Products

One house, 8 tools

edh.wtf is one house with 8 tools. Each tool is its own product, with its own name and colour. They share everything else, so any one of them reads as edh.wtf. 4 of them (Augur, ProxyPrintr, DeckboxPrintr, Deckwright) have no readable mark of their own yet and carry the edh.wtf mark in their colour until one reads.

edh.wtfType, neutrals and grounds
edh.wtfMark construction: gap and corner radius
edh.wtfGrid, book and voice rules
Each productName, descriptor and idea
Each productProduct mark in its colour (the house mark until its own reads)
Each productProduct colour, one family slot
Each productApplications: real output, where the product has one

The family colours

One colour per product, at the same strength as the edh.wtf blue, spaced round the colour wheel. A product colour never stands for a status: success, warning and error keep the interface colours.

Augur

Status: In development

Nothing joins a deck until you say yes.

Collection manager for Commander players who rebuild decks

Augur is the only Magic collection manager where an AI agent can propose changes to your cards, and no card joins or leaves a deck until you approve it.

Augur has no mark of its own yet (concepts A and C broke after three rounds each, and B reads the same as Scrywatch's mark). Until a drawing reads clearly, it uses the edh.wtf mark in Augur's colour, beside its name. Minimum size: the mark at 48 px, the lockup at 48 px tall. Below 48 px, such as a browser tab, use the small drawing, assets/mark-16.svg; the favicons are built from it. Clear space: a quarter of the mark's height on every side, kept free of type, edges and other marks. On a dark ground use the on-dark files; never recolour the mark in the brand colour on a busy picture.

Vizier

Status: Planned

Ask it the way you'd ask your pod.

Ask the edh.wtf tools in plain words.
